---
title: "Examples"
---

Five end-to-end walkthroughs, from raw data to a finished 3D visualization, each
reproducing a figure or workflow from the SciGraphs paper. If you want a single
panel explained control by control instead, use the
[Tutorials](../tutorials/panels/index.qmd) or the
[Panel Reference](../panels/overview.qmd).

| # | Example | You will learn |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [A combinatorial graph from a file](01-combinatorial-graph.qmd) | Import an edge list, lay it out, compute centrality and communities, and render. |
| 2 | [A geospatial flow map on a globe](02-geospatial-globe.qmd) | Geocode nodes, project onto a 3D globe, and draw geodesic arcs. |
| 3 | [An urban network on terrain](03-urban-terrain.qmd) | Download a street network with OSMnx, drape it onto DEM terrain, and add an amenity proximity graph. |
| 4 | [A sparse matrix from SuiteSparse](04-sparse-matrix.qmd) | Import a benchmark matrix, lay it out, and color by eigenvector centrality. |
| 5 | [A reproducible pipeline](05-reproducible-pipeline.qmd) | Capture a whole workflow in a declarative file, replay it with provenance, and drag a ready-to-run specification into Blender. |

## Before you begin

- Install and enable SciGraphs (see [Installation](../guide/installation.qmd)).
- Open the 3D Viewport sidebar with `N` and locate the **SciGraphs**, **OSMnx**,
  and **City2Graph** tabs.
- For the geospatial examples, Blender needs internet access.
